Subject: Proposal: Novalink — commercial and packaging clarifications

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising. Before we move to internal procurement, a couple of commercial questions from our side that will determine which path we take:

1) Credits vs. license unbundle: We need clarity on whether the "runtime credits" bucket can be used for all inference types (chat, embeddings, reranking) or if some workloads are excluded.

2) Unused credits: Does Redwood allow credit carry-forward between quarters if we commit to a multi-quarter pilot?

3) Packaging: We're evaluating a seat-based license + overage vs. pure consumption with upfront bridge credits. Do you have a simple side-by-side of the two options we can take to procurement?

If you can send a draft term sheet and any finance-friendly breakdown (month-by-month), that will help speed things up. I'm copying our procurement lead, Elena, who will coordinate the contract review.

Attachments: Novalink_RFP_Q3.pdf (reference)

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Novalink
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposal: Novalink — commercial and packaging clarifications

Sam — appreciate the questions and the quick follow. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short term sheet and a spreadsheet to make procurement's life easier.

- Runtime credits coverage: Credits apply to all tokenized inference (generation and embeddings). Reranking / specialized model hooks are supported as long as the model is in our catalog; custom on-prem plugins may be scoped separately.

- Carry-forward: For pilots we typically allow a single quarter roll-forward if a multi-quarter commitment is signed and usage variance is within the committed tolerance. For annual commitments we have a 10% bank that carries.

- Packaging options (summary):
  Option A — Consumption-first (recommended for variable workloads):
    * No seat license.
    * Pre-paid runtime credits with staged drawdown (Q1 onboarding credit, Q2 scaled commit).
    * Onboarding credits can be applied to egress and initial spikes.
  Option B — Seat + Overage (recommended if predictable, seat-local inference):
    * Seat licenses for core users plus lower per-token overage price.
    * Lower variability for finance but higher baseline.

I've attached a draft term sheet (draft-term-sheet.pdf) and a simple model (pricing-model.xlsx) that shows sample month-by-month P&L for both options. The workbook includes a scenario where we convert unused credits into a one-time services voucher for onboarding or training.

Proposed next steps:
- I can send a short MOU for the pilot today that includes a staged credit schedule.
- If procurement prefers seat + license numbers, Marissa can run a quick blended TCO and provide a proposed discount ladder.

Cc'ing Marissa and Stephanie for commercial/finance sign-off. Jordan will be looped in once you flag the preferred option for contract drafting.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: draft-term-sheet.pdf, pricing-model.xlsx

Thanks Karthik — that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement:

> From the draft: 'Onboarding credits can be applied to egress and initial spikes.'

Elena asked whether onboarding credits can also be used to offset data-transfer egress for our pilot (we have a large initial export). If not, we'd need an explicit egress credit line.

Also, on carry-forward: the single quarter roll-forward is ok, but procurement wants to confirm the mechanism — is it automatic if we sign an SOW, or must we execute an amendment?

Finally, do you have a defined cap on per-quarter consumption discounts if we exceed the committed tier? We want the safety of a ceiling rather than open-ended overage exposure.

If you can include a short mutual action plan with milestones and dates (pilot start, go/no-go review, contract execution), that will let us map internal approval gates.

Cheers,
Sam

Elena / Sam — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concrete commercial offer we can put in an MOU and then fold into a formal SOW / subscription:

Commercial offer (pilot → commit):
- 3-month pilot (90 days) with the following economics:
  * Q1 onboarding credit: $60,000 applied to runtime and egress (explicit credit line).
  * Q2 committed draw: $150,000 prepay that converts to a 20% discount vs. ad-hoc consumption.
  * Q3 optional committed month-to-month with carry-forward allowance: up to one quarter roll-forward of unused credits if a 12-month contract is signed by pilot close.
- Overage caps: Overages are charged, but we will cap monthly overage at 50% of the committed draw for the first two quarters post-pilot; after that standard terms apply.
- License carveout: If Novalink requests a seat-based license instead of consumption-only, we can provide a blended proposal: 10 seats + 40% discount on baseline token pricing with a lower overage rate; Marissa will share the blended TCO in the attached pricing model.

Operational / procurement details:
- Credit carry-forward: Mechanism is an amendment to the SOW that references the MOU credit ladder; our legal team will auto-generate the amendment if Novalink accepts the MOU within 30 days of pilot start.
- Egress credits: Explicit egress credit line will be documented (not auto-applied to other services).
- Mutual action plan (high level):
  1) Pilot kickoff — target: 2025-07-15 (prep + data handoff)
  2) Go/no-go checkpoint — target: 2025-09-12 (end of pilot review)
  3) Contract execution (if go) — target: 2025-09-30

Attachments: I've uploaded an updated pricing-model.xlsx with the blended seat scenario and a draft-term-sheet.pdf that includes the egress credit language. Jordan, can you take point on contract redlines once Novalink confirms option A or B? Stephanie, please confirm finance is comfortable with the 20% pilot-to-commit discount ladder and the 50% temporary overage cap.

If this looks ok I'll send a one-page MOU tonight for Elena to route. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk procurement through the credit mechanics — Sam, feel free to propose times.

Best regards,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
